title: Generalized Weakness
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a woman of childbearing age who presents with progressive generalized weakness that worsens with continued muscle use and improves with rest. She has developed ptosis, dysarthria, and dysphagia. Respiratory muscle involvement is present with mild hypoxemia from hypoventilation. Exam reveals fatigable weakness with preservation of sensation and reflexes — the hallmark of myasthenia gravis. The underlying pathophysiology is autoimmune antibody-mediated destruction of postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction. CT chest is essential to evaluate for thymoma, which is present in 10-15% of MG patients and whose resection can lead to remission in ~85%.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Determine how sick the patient looks.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: Investigate for lung pathology — respiratory muscle weakness can cause hypoventilation.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Investigate for cardiac pathology.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: Quick abdominal exam.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Genitalia
stacks.finding: Pelvic pain can present as abdominal pain — should be examined.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: HEENT / Neck
stacks.finding: Will show mild ptosis — key finding in MG.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Skin
stacks.finding: Look for rashes suggestive of autoimmune disease.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Extremities / Spine
stacks.finding: Look for edema or abnormalities given weakness symptoms.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych
stacks.finding: Neurological symptoms guide testing — fatigable weakness with preserved sensation and reflexes.

stacks.label: Chest X-ray
stacks.finding: Not required, but would be abnormal. May show anterior mediastinal mass.

stacks.label: CT chest with contrast / MRI chest
stacks.finding: CT chest is essential to rule out thymoma, seen in 10-15% of MG patients. Thymoma appears as anterior mediastinal mass.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: Good screening tool in nearly every patient.

stacks.label: ECG, 12 lead
stacks.finding: Generalized weakness can be cardiac. ECG rules out cardiac etiologies.

stacks.label: Pulse oximetry
stacks.finding: Oxygenation is lower than usual — likely from hypoventilation due to respiratory muscle weakness.

stacks.label: Sedimentation rate, erythrocyte
stacks.finding: Not required but would be abnormal in autoimmune disease.

stacks.label: HCG, beta (pregnancy test)
stacks.finding: All female patients of childbearing age should have pregnancy test before imaging and treatment.

stacks.label: TSH, serum
stacks.finding: Hypothyroidism is associated with generalized weakness — important to screen.

stacks.label: Acetylcholine receptor antibody, serum
stacks.finding: Positive detection strongly supports MG diagnosis. ~80% positive in generalized MG.

stacks.label: Electromyography
stacks.finding: EMG with repetitive stimulation shows decremental response — decreased signal with each stimulation. Differentiates from Lambert-Eaton (which shows incremental response).

stacks.label: Tensilon test
stacks.finding: Not required but would be positive in MG. Edrophonium temporarily improves muscle strength.

stacks.label: PT/PTT / INR
stacks.finding: Patient is likely to have surgery (thymectomy) — pre-surgical labs needed.

stacks.label: Type and screen / Type and Rh
stacks.finding: Pre-surgical labs for potential thymectomy.

stacks.label: Basic metabolic profile / Comprehensive metabolic profile / LFTs
stacks.finding: BMPs are excellent screening tools in any differential.

stacks.label: Methylprednisolone / Prednisone / Azathioprine
stacks.finding: Corticosteroids and azathioprine are first-line immunosuppressive treatments for MG.

stacks.label: Pyridostigmine / Neostigmine
stacks.finding: Pyridostigmine is for symptomatic treatment only — acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that increases ACh at neuromuscular junction. Does NOT treat underlying disease. Use in conjunction with immunosuppressants.

stacks.label: Consult surgery / Thymectomy
stacks.finding: Thymoma should be surgically removed. Thymectomy can lead to complete remission in ~85% of patients without further medication.

stacks.label: IVIG
stacks.finding: [Auto-split from bundled label "IVIG / Plasmapheresis"] Can be used pre-thymectomy for severe symptoms. However, expensive — conservative trial of steroids + pyridostigmine first is reasonable if patient is stable.

stacks.label: Plasmapheresis
stacks.finding: [Auto-split from bundled label "IVIG / Plasmapheresis"] Can be used pre-thymectomy for severe symptoms. However, expensive — conservative trial of steroids + pyridostigmine first is reasonable if patient is stable.

stacks.label: Instruct patient, smoking cessation
stacks.finding: One of the most important things for health — address smoking.

stacks.label: Advise patient, safe sex techniques
stacks.finding: Patient has history of STIs — review safe sex practices.

stacks.label: Reassure patient
stacks.finding: New chronic diagnosis causes anxiety — reassure and inform.

stacks.label: Papanicolaou smear
stacks.finding: HPV DNA test every 3 years for women ≥30. No history given — should be scheduled.

stacks.label: Tdap vaccine
stacks.finding: Tdap every 10 years. No history given — should be administered.

physical_exam.general: Generalized fatigable weakness. Worsens with continued use, improves with rest.
physical_exam.respiratory: Hypoventilation from respiratory muscle weakness. Decreased oxygen saturation. Monitor for myasthenic crisis.
physical_exam.neurological: Ptosis (eyelid drooping). Dysarthria. Dysphagia. Proximal asymmetric limb weakness. Fatigable weakness — repeat muscle testing worsens performance. Sensation and reflexes preserved. Differentiates from Lambert-Eaton and neuropathy.
physical_exam.heent: Mild ptosis. Facial muscle weakness may affect chewing and speech.

decoys.label: Intubation / mechanical ventilation (too early)
decoys.reason_wrong: Patient has respiratory muscle weakness but intubation is invasive and can often be avoided with medical management of MG first.

decoys.label: Pyridostigmine as monotherapy
decoys.reason_wrong: Pyridostigmine only treats symptoms. In a patient with respiratory involvement, immunosuppression (steroids/azathioprine) is needed to treat the underlying autoimmune process. Pyridostigmine also increases airway secretions.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies are positive in ~80% of generalized MG. EMG with repetitive stimulation shows decremental response (vs Lambert-Eaton which shows incremental).
Thymoma present in 10-15% of MG. CT chest with contrast mandatory in all new MG diagnoses.
Prednisone + azathioprine treat the underlying autoimmune process. First-line for moderate to severe MG.
Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor provides symptomatic relief but does NOT treat the disease. Use in conjunction with immunosuppression, not as monotherapy.
Surgical removal of thymoma. Can lead to remission in ~85% of patients.

case_summary: Myasthenia gravis with thymoma. Autoimmune antibodies against AChR → fatigable weakness. CT chest shows anterior mediastinal mass (thymoma, ~15% of MG). Treatment: steroids + pyridostigmine + thymectomy. Avoid pyridostigmine monotherapy in respiratory involvement.
